schemes.name: e-Shram (National Database of Unorganised Workers)
schemes.summary: Free government registration for unorganised, gig and platform workers. You get a Universal Account Number (UAN) card, which is the gateway to social security schemes.

eligibility_any_of.note: Unorganised workers aged 16-59, including gig and platform workers, who are not members of EPFO or ESIC and do not pay income tax.

benefits: e-Shram card with a 12-digit Universal Account Number (UAN), valid across India.
Registration is free.
Platform workers registered on e-Shram are to be covered for hospital care under Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY (announced in Union Budget 2025-26).
Helps the government reach you with social security schemes and help during emergencies.
how_to_apply: Self-register at eshram.gov.in using your Aadhaar number and the mobile number linked to Aadhaar.
Or visit a Common Service Centre (CSC) for free assisted registration.
Fill in occupation, address, education and bank account details, then download your e-Shram card.

schemes.name: Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan (PM-SYM)
schemes.summary: A voluntary pension scheme for unorganised workers. You pay a small monthly amount and the government pays the same amount into your pension.

eligibility_any_of.note: Unorganised workers aged 18-40 earning Rs 15,000 or less per month, with a savings bank or Jan Dhan account. Not for members of EPFO, ESIC or NPS, or income tax payers.

benefits: Assured pension of Rs 3,000 per month after age 60.
Monthly contribution of about Rs 55 to Rs 200, depending on your age when you join.
The government adds an equal (1:1) matching contribution.
If the subscriber dies after 60, the spouse gets 50% of the pension as family pension.
how_to_apply: Visit a Common Service Centre (CSC) with your Aadhaar and bank passbook, or apply online at maandhan.in.
Give consent for auto-debit of the monthly contribution from your bank account.
Keep the Shram Yogi pension card you receive.

schemes.name: Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY)
schemes.summary: Low-cost life insurance. If the insured person dies for any reason, the family gets Rs 2 lakh.

eligibility_any_of.note: People aged 18-50 with a savings bank or post office account who give consent for auto-debit.

benefits: Life cover of Rs 2 lakh for death due to any reason.
Premium of Rs 436 per year, auto-debited from your bank account.
Cover can continue up to age 55 if you keep paying the premium.
how_to_apply: Ask at your bank branch or post office, or use your bank's net banking / mobile app.
Fill the PMJJBY enrolment and consent-cum-declaration form and name a nominee.
Keep enough balance for the yearly auto-debit.

schemes.name: Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY)
schemes.summary: Very low-cost accident insurance, useful for anyone who works on the road.

eligibility_any_of.note: People aged 18-70 with a savings bank or post office account who give consent for auto-debit.

benefits: Rs 2 lakh for accidental death or full permanent disability.
Rs 1 lakh for partial permanent disability.
Premium of only Rs 20 per year, auto-debited from your bank account.
how_to_apply: Ask at your bank branch or post office, or use your bank's net banking / mobile app.
Fill the PMSBY enrolment and consent form and name a nominee.
Keep enough balance for the yearly auto-debit.

schemes.name: Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY)
schemes.summary: Free hospital treatment up to Rs 5 lakh per family per year at empanelled government and private hospitals.

eligibility_any_of.note: Online platform (gig) workers registered on e-Shram are to be covered, as announced in Union Budget 2025-26.
All senior citizens aged 70 and above are covered, irrespective of income.
Low-income families may already be listed under the SECC 2011 / state beneficiary lists. Check your name on the official beneficiary portal.

benefits: Cashless hospital treatment up to Rs 5 lakh per family per year.
Covers secondary and tertiary care hospitalisation at empanelled hospitals across India.
No limit on family size or age (for listed families).
how_to_apply: Check eligibility and make your Ayushman card at beneficiary.nha.gov.in or through the Ayushman app.
Or visit a Common Service Centre or an empanelled hospital's Ayushman Mitra desk.
Gig and platform workers should first register on e-Shram.

schemes.name: Code on Social Security, 2020 - rights of gig and platform workers
schemes.summary: A national labour law, in force from 21 November 2025, that for the first time recognises gig workers and platform workers and creates social security schemes and a fund for them.

eligibility_any_of.note: Applies to gig workers and platform workers who earn through apps or online platforms.

benefits: Legal definition of 'gig worker' and 'platform worker', so you are recognised by law.
The government can make schemes for life and disability cover, accident insurance, health and maternity benefits, old-age protection and creches for gig and platform workers.
Aggregators (platform companies) must contribute 1-2% of annual turnover to a Social Security Fund, capped at 5% of the amount paid to workers.
Gig and platform workers must be registered, with an Aadhaar-linked account so benefits can move with you across states.
Gig and platform workers have representatives on the National Social Security Board.
how_to_apply: Register on e-Shram so that you are counted and can receive these benefits.
Keep proof of your work on the platform (partner ID, payout statements).
For a dispute, use the platform's grievance officer first, then your state Labour Department.
